chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Billy Burns, Pastotis's wife and the Packard
summary: Butler enjoyed camel rides and Egyptian friends; he describes white trombonist Billy Burns's lavish lifestyle and his rivalry with Pastotis over Pastotis's Greek wife and a new Packard.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: The reason why Chitterson has been spoken of so much, Chitterson was the smallest man in the band and oh, we used to have some type of conspiracy and I was his buddy, I thought. So every night we were going to having camel rides, going to Cairo and seeing all the sights, the pyramids, and everything, all these lovely things, and I became very, very much attached to the Egyptians. They made me feel as I was one of them and I was trying to speak the language and I was learning fast, and this Mr. Pastotis (phonetic) he had a beautiful wife, Greek lady, and the trombone player, Billy Burns, he was a handsome fellow.

Billy Burns was a caucasian man, but Billy Burns had a pair of lips on him that looked like steak lips, and he didn't care nothing about what he looked like. He was sort of man, he knowed what he looked like. He didn't want to hear it, he wanted to be a black man. / So, we left Billy Burns alone. Billy Burns had some rich woman, I think she was something -- the fiancee of the Minister of Finance of Belgium and Billy Burns would give parties and you would go in -- the bathtub would be full of Channel's Crepe de chine,

and that's the way Billy Burns lived. He could afford all of these hotel bills of $35.00 a day. All right, then, Burns and he was doing his various things, had certain drugs and whatever they had, their pleasures. Arabian delights and he and Pastotis were great friends and it seems as though Pastotis' wife, seemed to like Burns very much.

Then Pastotis' wife was -- Pastotis had an old car, I think it was an old Ford or something and Burns sent and got a Packard, beautiful Packard. This is around 1936 and the Packard was a beautiful thing. Then Burns took the Packard off the boat and Pastotis got that devil look in him and then the lady got that love look on her for Burns.
